A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SimLTD research work. All ten pages of each support comparison of the text, equations, algorithms, figures, tables, and references. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v2 reports original SimLTD evaluations on LVIS and Objects365, transfer-learning experiments, and augmentation and fine-tuning ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and ablations, with revised scores for two SimLTD configurations in Table 2.

M1.justification: The three-stage framework, supervised and pseudo-label losses, frozen representations during tail adaptation, copy-paste augmentation, and detector fusion remain unchanged. Revised wording about random weights and exemplar replay describes procedures already present in v2.

E1.justification: Both versions retain LVIS and Objects365 evaluation, the COCO-to-LVIS transfer analysis, and COCO-unlabeled2017 and Objects365 unlabeled training sources. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Figure 1, Tables 2–3, and the Objects365 comparison in Figure 7. This includes the retained RichSem and Detic comparisons, CascadeMatch and FASA comparison, and NorCal baseline.

E3.justification: The reported splits, augmentations, metrics, training budgets, and fine-tuning settings remain unchanged. Figure 1 newly identifies its ResNet-50 setting, but neither version establishes a change to the underlying comparison protocol.

E4.justification: The transfer-learning analysis, pseudo-label examples, qualitative detections, augmentation ablations, and initialization and shot-count analyses are retained in Figures 4–6 and 8 and Table 4. Caption and wording edits introduce no new analysis.

E5.justification: Section 4.1 in both versions states that Dk is sampled three times with different random seeds and averaged metrics are reported. No change to repeated sampling or uncertainty reporting is documented.

E6.justification: Table 2 revises two SimLTD MixPL/DINO-R50 rows under unchanged reported settings. In (mAPbox, APr, APc, APf) order, Objects365-unlabeled changes from (38.3, 30.8, 37.5, 42.6) to (39.1, 31.5, 38.5, 43.1), and COCO-unlabeled2017 from (38.5, 31.6, 37.5, 42.5) to (39.4, 32.6, 38.5, 43.6). Figure 1 reflects the latter update. Other results remain unchanged; the reason for these revisions is not stated.

T1.justification: The dataset partition definitions, objectives in Equations (1)–(2), and mathematical description of transfer and fine-tuning are unchanged. Neither version adds formal results, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and main contributions retain the same claims about the three-stage framework, optional unlabeled data, architectural compatibility, and state-of-the-art LVIS performance. The conclusion is reworded without changing the paper's substantive contribution claims.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the same interpretations of representation transfer, pseudo-label imbalance, augmentation, and the fine-tuning trade-off. Applicability arguments and qualifications concerning rare instances, overfitting, and catastrophic forgetting are substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: Figure 1 newly specifies ResNet-50 for the plotted comparison, disclosing a setting previously unstated there. The implementation tools, hardware, training iterations, augmentation details, and open-source-code statement otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 51 references and substantive related-work discussion are retained. Positioning relative to multi-stage learning, few-shot detection, and methods requiring auxiliary labeled data is unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized wording and terminology edits, revises the fine-tuning paragraph and conclusion, and updates the arXiv stamp. Section order and overall narrative structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 adds a ResNet-50 legend qualifier and annotations showing +2.7 APr and +2.3 mAP over RichSem. Several captions are edited and Table 3 standardizes APFixed header capitalization. The existing figures and tables retain their placement and overall organization.

improvement.justification: Figure 1 now states the backbone setting and explicitly displays the margins over RichSem, making the headline comparison easier to assess. Local wording refinements provide a small additional clarity benefit. The improvement is limited to reporting: the unexplained Table 2 score revisions do not establish stronger scientific validation.
